draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Agumbe! It gets so much rain that people call it the Cherrapunji of South India, and the reserved forest here gets over 7,000 mm a year. This rainforest is also king cobra country, and there's a research station set up as a sanctuary for them.
draft.hungryLine: It's a small village, so keep it simple: local food at the bus stand hotel or Hotel Sri Ganesh, and vanilla tea with hot vadas at Bhattara tea.

moodReplies.show-me-around: The Agumbe Rainforest Research Station is about a 22 min walk away, and Jogigundi, a small waterfall, is just 10 to 15 minutes from the village.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Head to the sunset view point. On a clear day you can watch the sun drop into the Arabian Sea from 826 m up.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Barkana Falls near here drops 259 m, which makes it the 10th highest waterfall in India.

spots.name: Jogigundi
spots.detail: 10 to 15 min away · A small waterfall right next to Agumbe

spots.name: Koodlu theertha falls
spots.detail: 20 km away · A 3 to 4 km trek to a gorgeous waterfall

legends.title: The pounding stick falls
legends.body: In Kannada, onake means the pounding stick villagers use to pound grain. That's the name locals gave this waterfall near Agumbe.

tips.title: Pack for serious rain.
tips.body: Agumbe gets the highest rainfall in South India, so carry rain gear and expect wet trails.

tips.title: Stock up before you arrive.
tips.body: Food and drink options in the village are very limited, so bring what you need.

story.title: Malenadu forest
story.body: Agumbe sits in the thick forests of the Malenadu region of the Western Ghats, at about 660 m. It's part of a long forest corridor linking Kudremukh National Park and several wildlife sanctuaries.

story.title: Cherrapunji of the South
story.body: The rain here is so heavy that Agumbe earned the nickname Cherrapunji of South India. The reserved forest gets more than 7,000 mm in a year.

story.title: Home of the king cobra
story.body: The Agumbe Rainforest Research Station was set up inside the reserved forest as a sanctuary for the king cobra, Agumbe's flagship species. It works on research and conservation.

story.title: Treks and waterfalls
story.body: Today Agumbe is known for rainforest conservation, documenting medicinal plants, cottage industry and trekking. Visitors come for the falls and the sunset over the sea.

food.name: Hotel Sri Ganesh

food.name: Bhattara tea
